Ms. Archana Maheshwari - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Mayank Upadhyay - Advocate for the respondent [R-1
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant(s) assailing the impugned award dated 02.05.2023 passed by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 74/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.6,01,500/- along with interest has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Kalabai, who passed away in road traffic accident which occurred on 24.11.2021 involving the offending vehicle motorcycle M.P. 10 NA 8925.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellant(s) submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed as Rs.7325/- which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.8800/- .

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Learned counsel also submits that the Claims Tribunal has deducted 1/2 towards personal expenses whereas looking to the number of dependents 1/3rd should be deducted as per para-30 & 32 of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in Smt. Sarla Verma Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 24.11.2021 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.8800/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour'
and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs.
Mukesh Kumar Yadav, (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

Mukesh Kumar Yadav, (2022) 1 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the number of dependents 1/3rd is deducted.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Rs.8800/- x 12 - 1/3 x 7 Loss of Dependency:
(multiplier) = Rs.4,92,800/-
Medical, travelling, Special diet, Rs.84,500/-
 Attendant, Conventional heads  Funeral expenses Rs.16,500  Loss of estate Rs.16,500  Loss of love and affection (Husband) Rs.44,000  Loss of love and affection (son) Rs.44,000 Loss of love and affection (daughters) Rs.88,000/-
Total Amount: Rs.7,86,3  MACT Awarded: Rs.6,01,5  Enhanced Amount: Rs.1,84,8 6 .
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.7,86,300/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,01,500/-.
Accordingly, the appellant(s) are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.1,84,800/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8717 3 MA-4885-2023 7 .

The appeal is valued as Rs.1,00,000/- and for the rest of the amount, the claimant(s) will pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days from today and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.
In case the appellant(s) fails to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate, which was fixed in the impugned award and the other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
8 . Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off in above terms.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE soumya Sukhdev vs Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134380878/
